node.title: Filehandles and CSV_XS
node.author: Melly
node.doctext:
Hi Monks

I'm trying to understand the different behaviour of file-handles and similar (e.g. '').

I don't think I'd ever really thought about them - they just worked - but I ran into a problem with CSV_XS and getline. Basically, why does a FH variable work (e.g. $IN), but and don't.

The following code is non-functional without commenting out stuff, but should illustrate what I mean.

use Text::CSV_XS; my $csv = Text::CSV_XS->new(); open(my $IN, '<', 'test.csv'); # ok open(IN, '<', 'test.csv'); # nope my $row = $csv->getline(); # nope - Usage: Text::CSV_XS::getline(self, io) at test_02.pl line 11, line 2. my $row = $csv->getline(); # nope - Usage: Text::CSV_XS::getline(self, io) at test_02.pl line 11, line 2. my $row = $csv->getline($IN); # ok print ${$row}[0]; __DATA__ a,b,c d,e,f

So, what is the difference between "open(IN..." and "open($IN..."? (and is there a way to alias to, e.g., $DATA?)

UPDATE

Ah - \*DATA or \*IN - err, what does '\*' imply?
